content.title: Arts & Culture
content.summary: The Arvada Arts and Culture Commission aims to enhance the quality and accessibility of arts and cultural experiences in Arvada, Colorado, fostering community connection and supporting local artists. Their goals include deepening community attachment through the arts, investing in future cultural initiatives, creating diverse artistic experiences for all residents, and establishing a supportive environment for artists and the creative industry. Recent public art projects, such as murals at various underpasses, exemplify their commitment to expanding Arvada's public art collection.

![Abstract painting with round shapes in blues, greens, and yellows](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=5021)

![Arvada Arts and Culture Commission Logo](/ImageRepository/Document?documentId=4395)

***"We use the arts to create deeply connected communities."***

## Vision and Purpose

The Arvada Arts and Culture Commission is dedicated to developing the quality, quantity and accessibility of arts and cultural experiences for the Arvada, Colorado community.

The Commission brings people together and strengthens Arvada's sense of community, place and belonging by supporting and advocating for Arvada's artistic resources and cultural activities to make Arvada a home for working artists.

## Mission

The [Arvada Arts and Culture Commission](/249) (AACC) makes places that deepen community attachment, invests in the future of arts and culture, creates a diversity of arts experiences for all, and makes a home for artists and creative industry.

## Arvada's Public Art

The City of Arvada owns hundreds of pieces of art and is always looking for opportunities to expand its public art collect. Learn more about [Arvada's public art](/492).

### Some recent public art projects include:

- [Garrison Street Underpass Mural](/1114)
- [Quaker Street Underpass Mural](/1189)
- [Babe Walls Mural Refresh](/1191)
- [Allison Street Post Office Mural, 'La Letra'](/491)

## Goals of the Arvada Arts and Culture Commission

1. [Make Places that Deepen Community Attachment](#tabfe4c68ad-e46b-4476-b5e8-8f65d202d32c_0)

### **Guiding Theme: Building and improving quality of life by connecting neighbors to each other and to themselves through the arts**

- Explore options to link Olde Town Arvada and the Arvada Center through cross-promotion, collaborative programming and offerings, physical link, etc.
- Create a second cultural hub outside of Olde Town Arvada
- Lay the groundwork for Creative Arts District Designation by pursuing the "Call Yourself Creative" program through Colorado Creative Industries
- Make every neighborhood a place for arts and culture
- Designate city property for arts use and creative reuse

1. [Invest in the Future of Arts and Culture](#tabfe4c68ad-e46b-4476-b5e8-8f65d202d32c_1)

### **Guiding Theme: Provide a range of arts and culture services to residents and allocate sufficient resources to meet the growing and changing needs of our community**

- Create funds for public art by committing 1% of all capital projects over $50,000, create development fees program, and increasing general fund commitment to the AACC's public art program
- Create a City of Arvada dedicated staff position for Arts & Culture (half-time or more)
- Take lasting care of the art that Arvada has in its collection and that it acquires
- Build capacity and visibility in Colorado by having members of AACC and city staff members attend CCI conference, arts-relevant networking events, and broader arts-relevant trainings and events
- Build relationships with the business community, city departments, and non-profits to expand our impact and increase collaboration and engagement

1. [Create a Diversity of Arts Experiences for All](#tabfe4c68ad-e46b-4476-b5e8-8f65d202d32c_2)

### Guiding Theme: Embrace our small town traditions to achieve an inclusive, prosperous, creative, resilient community, and engage residents through the arts

- Ensure each resident is within a ten-minute walk of something artful
- Give all members of our diverse community a place at the table and opportunities for giving open feedback
- Increase Commission size from 9 to 11 members
- Support arts and cultural events through collaborations with other artists, organizations, boards and commissions, and city departments
- Celebrate diverse backgrounds, ideas, and perspectives in our community and beyond

1. [Make a Home for Artists and Creative Industry](#tabfe4c68ad-e46b-4476-b5e8-8f65d202d32c_3)

### Guiding Theme: Create a city where quality housing and creative work space is attainable to all

- Make Arvada one of the most artist-friendly cities on the Front Range through code changes and artist/city navigation information
- Identify the best processes to establish, encourage, and sustain affordable artist live/work/perform spaces
- Encourage artists and arts and culture-related business to relocate to the city
- Create and fund small grants program to support, forward, and encourage the work of artists and arts groups in our community
- Increase economic resiliency and workforce engagement by supporting creative industries

## Arvada Arts and Culture Commission Background

The Arvada Arts and Culture Commission was established by the Arvada City Council in 2015. The commission was formed during the [Arvada Center](https://arvadacenter.org/)'s transition from a City-operated organization to an independent non-profit.

The AACC consists of nine volunteer members from the Arvada community. The Commission meets monthly on Thursday evenings at Arvada City Hall. Recruitment to fill vacancies for the City of Arvada's boards and commissions begins each year in December. You can review the application process on the main [Boards, Commissions and Committees page](https://www.arvadaco.gov/248/Boards-Commissions-and-Committees).
